AccountKind.description:
What kind of account this is.

Explicit string values: the kind is persisted, so reordering the members
must not rewrite anybody's data.
AccountKind.title: AccountKind

AccountKindOption.description:
An account kind, and which side of net worth it lands on.

`category` is derived from the kind and never chosen, so a client can
group the dropdown — and say "money you owe" against a balance — without
duplicating the rule that decides it.
AccountKindOption.title: AccountKindOption

AliasResponse.description: One child: a spelling that resolves to this merchant.
AliasResponse.title: AliasResponse

CatalogOption.description: One admissible value, and something to put beside it in a dropdown.
CatalogOption.title: CatalogOption

EditTransactionPayload.description:
A correction. Everything omitted is left alone.

On a movement that came from a bank alert, the first correction keeps what
the bank said: `stated` on the response is how a reader tells the two
apart afterwards.
EditTransactionPayload.title: EditTransactionPayload

EnterTransactionPayload.description: Money that moved without an alert to announce it.
EnterTransactionPayload.title: EnterTransactionPayload

FinancialCatalogResponse.description:
Every vocabulary this context's endpoints accept.

`instrument_kinds` is the one that is not an account kind and is the one
people reach for anyway: a savings account is `savings`, but the alerts it
sends name the instrument `account`. Offer it as its own list, never a
text field.
FinancialCatalogResponse.title: FinancialCatalogResponse

InboxSendersPayload.description:
The senders approved for the caller's one forwarding address.

No address here — it is assigned automatically and never chosen by a
caller. Both lists may be empty, which approves nothing: a forwarding
address with no approved sender reads nothing, the safe default rather
than a broken one.
InboxSendersPayload.title: InboxSendersPayload

IngestionCatalogResponse.description:
Ingestion's vocabulary, for the screens that render or filter by it.

`instrument_kinds` is the one a client sends rather than displays, and it
is published from here rather than from Financial because these are the
words a bank alert arrives with. An account declared with any other
spelling is accepted and then never matches an alert — silently, since
nothing about that is an error.
IngestionCatalogResponse.title: IngestionCatalogResponse

InstrumentKind.description:
The sort of card or account a movement arrived through.

Financial's own vocabulary, mapped at the boundary from whatever the
publishing context calls its instruments — the same arrangement as
`MovementDirection`. Neither context gets to change the other's meaning by
editing its own.

Not the same thing as `AccountKind`, and the difference is the whole point
of this type existing. `AccountKind` is what the owner calls the account;
this is what the *bank* calls the thing the money moved through, and only
these words ever appear in an alert. A savings account is declared
`SAVINGS` and its transfers arrive as `ACCOUNT` — spelling the fingerprint
with the account kind produces a key no alert can ever match, and the
owner finds out only by noticing that nothing was ever assigned.
InstrumentKind.title: InstrumentKind

LinkInstrumentPayload.description:
Teach an account another of the names its alerts arrive under.

One real account emails as a debit card for purchases and as an account
number for transfers, under different last four digits. Both have to be
linked or half its movements wait forever.
LinkInstrumentPayload.title: LinkInstrumentPayload

MerchantCatalogResponse.description:
Every vocabulary this context's endpoints accept or return.

`categories` repeats what `GET /merchants/categories` already answers.
That endpoint stays: it is what a client already calls, and one list in
two places costs nothing next to breaking it.
MerchantCatalogResponse.title: MerchantCatalogResponse

MerchantCategory.description:
What kind of spending this merchant represents.

Explicit string values: the category is persisted and shown in a dropdown,
so reordering the members must not rewrite anybody's data.
MerchantCategory.title: MerchantCategory

MergeMerchantsPayload.description: The merchant in the path survives and takes everything this one had.
MergeMerchantsPayload.title: MergeMerchantsPayload

MoveAliasPayload.description: Reattach one child to a different parent.
MoveAliasPayload.title: MoveAliasPayload

MovementDirection.description:
Which way the money went, in Financial's own vocabulary.

Ingestion has an enum that happens to look identical today. Mapping
between them at the boundary is the point: neither context gets to change
the other's meaning by editing its own.
MovementDirection.title: MovementDirection

NotificationResponse.description:
One arrival. No body: a list never shows the email itself, and two of
the states below discarded theirs on purpose.
NotificationResponse.title: NotificationResponse

OpenAccountPayload.description:
Declare an account.

Give it an instrument and every alert arriving under that bank and those
last four digits lands here — including the ones that already arrived and
have been waiting. Leave it out for what never emails: cash, a mortgage.
OpenAccountPayload.title: OpenAccountPayload

ProcessingStatus.description:
Explicit string values: this enum is persisted and serialized, so the
stored representation must survive a reordering of the members.
ProcessingStatus.title: ProcessingStatus

RegisterPayload.description:
Registration, plus the same optional sender approval `PATCH
/identity/inbox` accepts — set here to skip a second call, or leave
empty and approve senders later. The forwarding address itself is
assigned regardless of whether any sender is named here.
RegisterPayload.title: RegisterPayload

RestateBalancePayload.description:
What the account holds **now** — the figure the bank shows today.

Not the opening balance: that one is derived from this and the movements
already recorded, because it is the half nobody can look up. Signed, so
an overdrawn account and an overpaid card can both be stated.
RestateBalancePayload.title: RestateBalancePayload

SetCreditLimitPayload.description: State or restate what a card may owe. `null` clears it.
SetCreditLimitPayload.title: SetCreditLimitPayload

SetupStepResponse.description:
One step of connecting a bank.

`at` is null for the two steps that are states rather than events (the
address exists, somebody is approved) — and for any step still open.
SetupStepResponse.title: SetupStepResponse

SplitAliasPayload.description: Pull one child out into a merchant of its own.
SplitAliasPayload.title: SplitAliasPayload

StatedResponse.description: What the bank said, before anybody corrected it.
StatedResponse.title: StatedResponse

TransactionOrigin.description:
Where a movement came from, which decides what may be trusted about it.

A bank alert states a fact somebody else recorded; a manual entry is the
user's own claim. Automatic payments that never email are exactly why the
second exists.
TransactionOrigin.title: TransactionOrigin

personal_finance__contexts__financial__p.description:
The canonical merchant behind this movement's counterparty text.

Joined when the answer is read, never stored on the movement: the grouping
belongs to Merchant and a user can change it, so a rename or a merge shows
up on every past movement at once with nothing to re-process.
personal_finance__contexts__financial__p.title: MerchantResponse

put.description:
Correct what this account holds, without touching a single movement.

For the ordinary case of declaring an account and not knowing what it
held before the alerts Finflow already has: open it at zero, then send
the figure the bank shows today. The opening balance is solved backwards
so the ledger still adds up to it, every movement keeps counting exactly
once, and net worth follows from the corrected number.

PUT because the body carries the whole fact. Allowed on a closed account:
correcting what was already there is not new money moving.

post.description:
Stop taking movements, keeping the history and the balance.

Not a delete: a closed account still explains past spending, and a
paid-off loan closing at zero is exactly what should stay visible.

put.description:
State or restate what this card may owe.

PUT rather than PATCH: the body carries the whole fact, and sending no
limit clears it rather than leaving the old one in place.

post.description:
Add another card or account number whose alerts belong here.

One real account emails as a debit card for purchases and as an account
number for transfers. Linking is always the owner's call — inferring it
would be guessing about somebody's money — and it adopts the movements
already waiting under that key.

get.description:
What a client may send, so a form cannot offer what the API rejects.

Unauthenticated like the merchant catalogue beside it: this is the shape
of the API, not anybody's data, and a client needs it to render the form
that a session is created from.

Assets minus liabilities, one figure per currency held.

Empty for somebody who declared no accounts, which is an ordinary answer:
they are watching what comes in and goes out, not a net position.

schema.title: Response Get Net Worth Financial Net Worth Get

get.description:
What a period adds up to, broken down by month, category, merchant or
account — and totalled per currency, never across them.

It takes the same filters as `/transactions`, so any bucket here can be
opened as a list by repeating the query with the bucket's key. `timezone`
only affects `month`, and it matters: a purchase at 8pm on the 31st falls
in the next month once it is read in UTC.

Movements, newest first, each with the merchant behind its text.

`merchant_id` and `category` are Merchant's answer, so a movement whose
counterparty nobody has resolved yet matches neither — it is unknown, not
uncategorized. `from` is included and `to` is not, so two consecutive
months can be asked for without one movement landing in both.

post.description:
Record money the bank never emailed about.

An automatic payment, cash, a transfer that produced no alert. The account
is optional: somebody watching only what comes in and goes out has none.

get.description:
Alive, and which deployment this is.

The environment is here because the only other way to tell two stacks
apart is the URL, and a URL is exactly what gets pasted into the wrong
command. Anything about to write — `scripts/smoke.py` above all — asks the
deployment itself rather than trusting the env file it happened to load.

The caller's forwarding address, and who is currently approved to send
to it. Whose inbox to read comes from the verified token, never from the
request.

patch.description:
Replace who may send to the caller's forwarding address.

A full replacement, not a merge: the lists sent here become the whole
approved set. Leave both empty and the address is approved for nobody —
connected in the sense of existing, but reading nothing.

post.description:
Create an account and assign it a forwarding address.

The address itself never appears in this response — it depends only on
the new account's id, so `GET /identity/inbox` right after this call
already has it.

get.description: What this context's states are called, and what an instrument may be.

The caller's bank mail, newest first.

An empty list is an ordinary answer: it means nothing has been forwarded
yet, or the forwarding rule is not doing what its owner thinks it is.
The caller's four steps, which of them are done, and what is next.
What a client may send, and what the words in a response mean.
The category vocabulary, for a dropdown that cannot drift from it.

patch.description:
Rename a merchant, recategorize it, or both.

Either counts as reviewing it: a user who named a merchant has looked at
what it is, so it leaves the review queue.

post.description:
Move one spelling to another merchant, and return the new parent.

The correction is permanent: from here on that spelling resolves by exact
match, and no rule re-derives where it belongs.
Pull one spelling out into a merchant of its own, and return it.
Accept a merchant as it stands, guessed children included.
Fold one merchant into the one named in the path, which survives.
